newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares hit by weak regional confidence.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares hit by weak regional confidence.

text.p: Weak confidence in Southeast Asia, exacerbated by regional currency volatility, pushed Singapore stocks lower on Monday, dealers said.
"Singapore suffers from a lack of (fund) flow and the regional currencies problem is not helping at all," said one. "Funds are staying away from the region, not just Singapore."
Southeast Asian currencies went on a roller-coaster ride on Monday as devaluation fears spread following the effective devaluations of the peso and baht.
Singapore dollar fell to a low of 1.444 to the U.S. dollar from 1.4395 earlier on Monday.

After touching a low of 1,951.71, the Straits Times Industrials index ended at 1,954.60, down 12.54 points. It was dragged down by shiprepair group Keppel Corp and property developer Wing Tai Holdings.
Keppel fell 35 cents to S$6.20 after announcing plans over the weekend to raise US$350 million. Sentiment was further dampened by expectations of weak interim results.
Banks, which received an early boost from a pro-financial sector budget announced on Friday, also succumbed. DBS foreign units ended S$0.30 down at S$18.80 after hitting S$19.40.
Most electronic counters, led by Creative, Flextech and Electronics Resources, bucked the downtrend, pushing the SES electronics index up 1.78 points to end at 131.11.
